en: to be verified; to be demonstrated

examples.en: It was proven that what he said is true.
This medicine's effect is proven by experiments.
If his innocence is proven, he'll be released right away.

examples.ko: 아직 입증되지 않은 이야기는 믿지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't believe stories that haven't been proven yet.

examples.ko: 연구를 통해 운동이 기억력에 좋다는 것이 입증되었어요.
examples.en: Research has shown that exercise is good for memory.
He's a player whose skill has been proven, so everyone expects a lot.

explain: '증명되다'와 비슷하지만 법정, 연구, 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 수학 문제는 '증명하다', 사실이나 효과, 실력은 '입증하다'를 써요. 반대로 '입증되지 않았다'는 아직 확인이 안 됐다는 말이에요. 능동형은 '입증하다'예요.

phrases.en: The research team proved the drug's effect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능동형으로, 증명하는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, with the person proving as the subject.

phrases.en: That story hasn't been verified yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 확인이 안 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it has not been confirmed yet.

phrases.en: His skill has been proven.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 넓게 쓰는 말이고 수학에서도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that is also used in math.

explain_en: Shown true using evidence; claims, effects, facts. It is similar to 증명되다 and is often used in courtrooms, research, and news. Math is 증명하다, while facts, effects, and ability are 입증하다. '입증되지 않았다' means it has not been confirmed yet. The active form is 입증하다.

gh: shown true by logic or proof

p.n: 입증 is common for evidence in law and research; 증명 is more general.

t90.ax: It was proven that what he said is true.

examples.en: My father subscribes to an architecture trade magazine.
This article was published in a medical journal.

examples.ko: 전문지에는 일반 잡지보다 어려운 말이 많아요.
examples.en: Specialist magazines have more difficult words than general ones.

examples.ko: 전문지 기자로 일한 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been five years since I started as a trade magazine reporter.

examples.ko: 그 분야 전문지를 읽으면 최신 소식을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: Reading that field's trade magazine tells you the latest news.

examples.ko: 전문지에 글을 실으려면 심사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To publish in a specialist magazine, you must pass a review.

explain: 앞에 분야 이름을 붙여서 '의학 전문지', '컴퓨터 전문지'라고 해요. 여러 분야를 다루는 신문은 '종합지'라고 해서 짝이 돼요. 그 일을 하는 사람이 많이 읽어서 말이 조금 어려워요.

phrases.en: My older brother likes reading computer trade magazines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 분야 이름을 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A field name goes in front.

phrases.en: I read a specialist magazine in my field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 일을 하는 사람들이 보는 잡지를 읽는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means reading a magazine made for people in that line of work.

phrases.en: General papers and specialist magazines have very different content.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 분야를 다루는 종합지와 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to contrast with 종합지, which covers many fields.

explain_en: Put the field before it: '의학 전문지', '컴퓨터 전문지'. Its counterpart is '종합지', which covers many fields. Readers are mostly people in that line of work, so the language is a little harder.

examples.en: My uncle works in the politics desk of a newspaper.
A politics reporter delivered the news from the National Assembly.
I want to work in the society desk rather than the politics desk.
The broadcaster's politics desk got busy from dawn.
A reporter from the politics desk published a book.

examples.ko: 정치부 기사는 뉴스 맨 앞에 나올 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Politics desk stories often come at the front of the news.

explain: 신문사나 방송국에서 정치 소식을 맡는 부서예요. 다른 부서로는 '사회부', '경제부', '문화부', '스포츠부'가 있어요. 뒤에 '기자'를 붙여 '정치부 기자'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The head of the politics desk held a meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부서의 책임자를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person in charge of the desk.

phrases.en: My friend works in the society desk at a broadcaster.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정치부와 같은 층위에 있는 다른 부서 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of another desk at the same level as 정치부.

phrases.en: That anchor came from the politics desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전에 정치부에서 일한 사람을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce someone who formerly worked on the desk.

explain_en: The department at a newspaper or broadcaster that covers political news. Other desks include 사회부, 경제부, 문화부 and 스포츠부. It is often used before 기자, as in 정치부 기자.

examples.en: Try finding the minimum value in this graph.
Today's minimum temperature was five degrees below zero.
Please calculate what the minimum value is.

examples.ko: 최솟값보다 작은 수는 입력할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't enter a number smaller than the minimum value.
Find the difference between the minimum and maximum values.
I wrote code that finds the minimum value in an array.

explain: 반대말은 '최댓값'이고, 수학이나 통계, 프로그래밍 수업에서 많이 나와요. 맞춤법으로는 사이시옷을 넣어 '최솟값'으로 적어요. 일상에서는 '가장 작은 값'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I found the minimum value of the function.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학 문제에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in math problems.

phrases.en: Mark the minimum and maximum values on the graph.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말과 함께 짝으로 외워 두면 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easy to remember as a pair with its opposite.

phrases.example: 이 숫자들 중에서 가장 작은 값을 찾으세요.
phrases.en: Find the smallest value among these numbers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '최솟값'을 풀어서 쉽게 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say 'minimum'.

explain_en: Minimum value of a function or data set — math, school. The opposite is '최댓값', and it appears often in math, statistics and programming classes. The standard spelling includes the sai-siot, '최솟값'. In everyday talk people may say '가장 작은 값' instead.

t90.ax: Please calculate what the minimum value is.

examples.en: Metal was detected at the airport security check.
A strange signal was picked up on the radar.
When smoke is detected, an alarm sounds.
The rescue team set out for the detected location.
I was relieved because no virus was detected.

examples.ko: 소리가 너무 작아 탐지될 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The sound was too faint to be detected.

explain: 숨어 있거나 잘 안 보이는 것을 기계나 장치가 찾아낼 때 써요. 사람이 눈으로 찾을 때는 '발견되다'가 자연스러워요. 능동은 '탐지하다'이고, '탐지기', '탐지견'처럼 다른 말과 붙여서도 써요.

phrases.en: The virus was not detected in the test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 아무것도 찾지 못했을 때 부정형으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when a device finds nothing.

phrases.en: I installed a smoke detector in my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탐지기'는 무언가를 찾아내는 장치를 말하고 다른 말 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '탐지기' means a detecting device and attaches to other nouns.

phrases.en: A small crack was found in the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 눈으로 찾았을 때는 '탐지되다'보다 '발견되다'가 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: When a person finds something by eye, '발견되다' is more natural than '탐지되다'.

explain_en: Passive: something gets sensed by a device (금속이 탐지되다) It is used when a machine or device finds something hidden or hard to see. When a person finds something by eye, '발견되다' sounds more natural. The active form is '탐지하다', and it also joins other words, as in '탐지기' (detector) and '탐지견' (detection dog).

en: to be written; to be marked; to be labeled

examples.en: The price is marked next to the product.
The name is written in both Hangul and English.
The expiration date is printed on the back of the package.

examples.ko: 지도에 표기된 길로 갔더니 공원이 나왔어요.
examples.en: I took the route marked on the map and came to a park.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 발음과 다르게 표기될 때가 많아요.
examples.en: This word is often spelled differently from how it sounds.
The country of origin was written so small that it was hard to check.

explain: '쓰여 있다'보다 딱딱하고, 포장지, 지도, 안내문에 정해진 방식으로 적혀 있을 때 써요. '한글 표기', '영어 표기'처럼 명사 '표기'도 자주 나와요. 직접 손으로 쓰는 일에는 '쓰다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The expiration date is marked on the back of the package.
phrases.nuance_ko: '표기되다'보다 이미 적혀 있는 상태를 말할 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of already being written, rather than the act of being written.

phrases.en: The place name was marked incorrectly on the map.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자나 이름이 틀리게 적혔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a letter or name was written wrongly.

phrases.en: How is this name written in English?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 글자나 언어로 적는지 물을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to ask which script or language something is written in.

explain_en: Shown by label or spelling notation, like prices on packaging. It is stiffer than 쓰여 있다 and fits things shown in a set way on packaging, maps, or notices. The noun 표기, as in 한글 표기, is also common. For writing by hand, 쓰다 sounds more natural.

dis.h: shown by label or spelling notation
gh: a whole document is drawn up
stated or listed in a document, formal
gets written down; plain everyday word

p.n: Shown as a label versus written down.

t90.ax: The price is marked next to the product.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 거포 타자가 한 명 있어요.
examples.en: Our team has one big slugger.
That player grew into a power hitter this year.

examples.ko: 거포가 들어오면서 팀 득점이 크게 늘었어요.
examples.en: Since the slugger joined, the team's scoring has gone up a lot.
Even if he's a slugger, too many strikeouts are a problem.

examples.ko: 그는 홈런을 마흔 개나 친 리그 최고의 거포예요.
examples.en: He is the league's top slugger, with forty home runs.

examples.ko: 이번 시즌에 거포 유망주가 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many promising sluggers appeared this season.

explain: 야구에서 홈런을 펑펑 치는 타자를 말할 때 주로 써요. 정확하게 안타를 치는 '교타자'와 반대 느낌이고, 스포츠 뉴스에서 '거포 유망주'처럼 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 팀은 거포 유망주를 여러 명 키우고 있어요.
phrases.en: That team is developing several promising sluggers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구 뉴스에서 홈런을 많이 칠 것 같은 젊은 선수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in baseball news for a young player expected to hit many home runs.

phrases.example: 그는 정확하기보다 힘이 센 거포형 타자예요.
phrases.en: He is a power-type hitter rather than a precise one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-형'이 붙으면 타자의 스타일을 설명하는 느낌이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-형' describes the hitter's style or type.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 몇 년 만에 거포가 됐어요.
phrases.en: That player became a slugger in a few years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선수가 성장해서 홈런을 많이 치게 된 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a player who has grown into a home run hitter.

explain_en: It is mostly used in baseball for a batter who hits lots of home runs. It contrasts with a '교타자', a contact hitter, and appears in sports news in phrases like '거포 유망주' (slugger prospect).

en: to be renewed; to be updated; to be broken as a record

examples.ko: 올해 여름 최고 기온 기록이 경신됐어요.
examples.en: This summer's record high temperature was broken.
The world record in track and field was broken again.

examples.ko: 판매 기록이 경신될 때마다 직원들이 기뻐해요.
examples.en: Every time the sales record is broken, the staff are happy.

examples.ko: 이 영화의 관객 수 기록은 곧 경신될 거예요.
examples.en: This movie's attendance record will be broken soon.

examples.ko: 기록이 경신된 날 선수들은 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: On the day the record was broken, the players cried.

examples.ko: 최저 기온 기록이 경신돼서 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The record low temperature was broken and it was on the news.

explain: 거의 항상 '기록'과 같이 써서 '기록이 경신되다'라고 해요. 기록을 깨는 사람이 주어이면 '기록을 경신하다'가 돼요. 일상에서는 '기록이 깨지다'가 더 흔해요. 계약이나 여권을 새로 바꾸는 것은 소리가 비슷한 '갱신하다'라고 해서 달라요.

phrases.en: That athlete broke the world record.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기록을 깨는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person who breaks the record is the subject.

phrases.en: This summer's heat record was broken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning and more natural in everyday talk.
phrases.en_equiv: for a record to be broken

phrases.example: 이번 대회에서 기록이 경신될 것 같아요.
phrases.en: It looks like the record will be broken at this contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~ㄹ 것 같다'로 앞으로의 일을 짐작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -ㄹ 것 같다 to guess about something that may happen.
phrases.en_equiv: it seems the record will be renewed

explain_en: Mostly records being broken (기록 경신), news and sports style. It almost always goes with 기록, as in '기록이 경신되다'. When the person who breaks it is the subject, it becomes '기록을 경신하다'. In daily talk '기록이 깨지다' is more common. Renewing a contract or passport uses the similar-sounding but different word '갱신하다'.

t90.ax: This summer's record high temperature was broken.

examples.en: That writer won a literary award this year.
I bought the award-winning book at the bookstore.
Our school gives a literary award to students every year.

examples.ko: 제 꿈은 신인 문학상에 당선되는 거예요.
examples.en: My dream is to win a new writers' literary award.

examples.ko: 문학상 후보에 오른 소설을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm reading a novel nominated for the literary award.

examples.ko: 이번 문학상은 시 부문 심사가 어려웠대요.
examples.en: I heard judging the poetry category was hard for this award.

explain: '문학상을 받다', '문학상에 당선되다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 달라요. '노벨 문학상'처럼 이름 앞에 붙여서 말해요. 시, 소설 같은 글을 쓰는 사람이 받는 상이에요.

phrases.en: That writer won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상 이름 앞에 붙여 가장 유명한 문학상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before the prize name to refer to the most famous literary award.

phrases.en: This year's literary award winner was announced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 받은 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who won the award.

phrases.en: His novel won a literary award.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 내서 뽑혔을 때는 '받다'보다 '당선되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a submitted work being chosen, use '당선되다' instead of '받다'.

explain_en: The verbs change with context: 문학상을 받다 for receiving it, 문학상에 당선되다 for winning a contest. It attaches to names, as in 노벨 문학상. It is given to people who write poetry, fiction, and similar works.

en: to be excavated; to be dug; to be discovered

examples.en: The ruins of an ancient city were excavated from underground.
Old bowls were unearthed during construction.
New talent gets discovered at this contest.
Excavated relics are displayed in the museum.
There are many tombs that haven't been excavated yet.
That singer was discovered on the street and became famous.

explain: 땅속의 유물이나 숨은 재능을 찾아 드러낼 때 써요. '발견되다'는 우연히 보게 된 느낌이고, '발굴되다'는 파거나 찾는 노력 끝에 나온다는 느낌이에요. 사람에게는 '발탁되다'와도 비교해 보세요.

phrases.en: New talent was discovered at the audition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨은 재능 있는 사람을 찾아낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone with hidden talent is found.

phrases.example: 그 지역에서 옛 유물이 계속 발굴되고 있어요.
phrases.en: Old relics are still being excavated in that area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작업이 아직 진행 중일 때 '-고 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-고 있다' when the work is still in progress.

phrases.en: That tomb has not been excavated yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 파거나 찾아내지 못했을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when it has not yet been dug up or found.

explain_en: Dug up or newly found, also for talent or hidden things. It is used when relics underground or hidden talent are found and brought out. 발견되다 feels like something noticed by chance; 발굴되다 comes after digging or searching effort. For people, compare it with 발탁되다.

t90.ax: New talent gets discovered at this contest.

en: to broadcast live; to relay live

examples.ko: 기자는 불이 난 현장의 상황을 생중계하고 있어요.
examples.en: The reporter is broadcasting the situation at the fire scene live.
The broadcaster airs the final live from start to finish.
Today's opening ceremony was also broadcast live online.
The mayor decided to broadcast the meeting live.
They will broadcast the concert live on this channel.

examples.ko: 현장을 생중계하면 많은 사람이 바로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you broadcast the scene live, many people can watch right away.

explain: '경기를 생중계하다', '행사를 생중계하다'처럼 현장에서 일어나는 일을 그 자리에서 바로 보여 준다는 느낌으로 써요. '생중계를 하다'로 나누어 말해도 같은 뜻이에요. 방송국, 기자, 개인 채널 모두 주어가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Please broadcast this event live.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 표제어는 기본형이라서 말할 때는 이렇게 활용해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make a polite request; the headword is the dictionary form.

phrases.en: The station broadcast the opening ceremony live yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 끝난 일을 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for something that has already happened.

phrases.en: I can see the reporter broadcasting live from the scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -는 lets it modify a following noun.

explain_en: Live relay of an outside event, such as sports or news. It is used for showing what is happening on the spot right away, as in '경기를 생중계하다' or '행사를 생중계하다'. You can split it as '생중계를 하다' with the same meaning. The subject can be a broadcaster, a reporter or a personal channel.

t90.ax: The mayor decided to broadcast the meeting live.

en: to be owned; to be kept

examples.en: That painting is kept in the national museum.
This book was added to the university library's collection.
The works in the collection number over three thousand.
I heard that an old map is held in the collection.
Experts examine works first before they enter the collection.

examples.ko: 이 유물은 내년부터 새 건물에 소장될 거예요.
examples.en: This relic will be housed in the new building from next year.

explain: '소장'은 박물관·도서관·개인이 귀한 것을 보관하는 것이에요. '보관되다'보다 귀한 작품이나 책에 어울려요. 물건을 모아 두는 쪽은 '소장하다'예요.

phrases.en: I went to see the works kept in the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박물관 등에서 귀하게 보관하는 작품을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to valued works held in a museum or similar place.

phrases.example: 그 책은 우리 학교 도서관에 소장되어 있지 않아요.
phrases.en: That book is not in our school library's collection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도서관에 그 자료가 없다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to say a library does not have that item.
phrases.en_equiv: is not held in the collection

phrases.en: This painting is part of the museum's collection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보관하고 있는 귀한 물건을 부르는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This noun names a valued item that is kept in a collection.

explain_en: Passive; items kept in a museum or library (박물관에 소장되다) '소장' means a museum, library, or individual keeping something valuable. It fits precious works and books more than '보관되다' does. The side that keeps the collection uses '소장하다'.

dis.h: be kept in a museum or collection

en: to be submitted; to be entered

examples.en: That film was entered in a film festival.
My photo will be entered in the contest.

examples.ko: 올해 박람회에는 새 제품이 많이 출품돼요.
examples.en: Many new products are exhibited at this year's expo.
I went and saw all of the submitted works.
That novel could not be entered for the literary prize.
I'm glad my work was entered in the exhibition.

explain: '출품하다'는 내놓는 쪽, '출품되다'는 내놓아지는 쪽 이야기예요. 영화제·공모전·전시회·박람회 앞에 '~에'를 붙여요. 주어는 사진, 영화, 그림 같은 작품이에요. 학교 대회에 낼 때는 보통 '내다', '제출하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 그림은 다음 달 전시회에 출품될 거예요.
phrases.en: That painting will be submitted to the exhibition next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에' 앞에 전시회, 영화제 같은 장소나 행사가 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The event, such as an exhibition or film festival, comes before '에'.
phrases.en_equiv: to be submitted to an exhibition

phrases.en: That work was not submitted to the contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품이 내놓아지지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that a work was not entered.

phrases.en: There are a hundred submitted works in total.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회나 전시에 낸 작품을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the works that were entered in a contest or show.

explain_en: Passive: a work is sent to an exhibition or contest. '출품하다' is told from the side that puts a work forward, and '출품되다' from the side of the work being put forward. Add '~에' after a film festival, contest, exhibition, or expo. The subject is a work such as a photo, film, or painting. For a school competition people usually say '내다' or '제출하다'.

t90.ax: My photo will be entered in the contest.

examples.en: They found a gold vein in the mountains.
I heard there is a large mineral vein in this area.
A mineral vein runs long underground.
Copper came out of the new vein.

examples.ko: 광맥까지 파 내려가는 데 몇 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took months to dig down to the vein.
People wandered the mountains looking for a vein of ore.

explain: 광석이 줄기처럼 길게 모여 묻혀 있는 곳을 말해요. '금광맥', '철광맥'처럼 앞에 광물 이름을 붙여 쓰기도 해요. 보통 '광맥을 찾다', '광맥을 발견하다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그들은 몇 년 동안 광맥을 찾았어요.
phrases.en: They searched for a mineral vein for years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광석이 묻힌 곳을 찾아다닐 때 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for looking for where ore is buried.
phrases.en_equiv: to look for a mineral vein

phrases.en: An iron vein was found in this mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광맥' 앞에 광물 이름을 붙이면 어떤 광석인지 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting a mineral name before 'gwangmaek' tells which ore it is.

phrases.en: They dug a tunnel underground along the vein.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄기처럼 이어진 광맥의 모양을 살려서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the stream-like shape of a vein: following it as it runs.

explain_en: Underground seam of ore, mining; also figurative rich source. It is a place where ore lies buried in a long, stream-like line. You can put a mineral name before it, as in '금광맥' (gold vein) and '철광맥' (iron vein). The usual patterns are '광맥을 찾다' and '광맥을 발견하다'.
